classification: formal-fleet allocation-law correction (scheduling layer). Retires per-family contiguous candidate-window ownership; adopts canonical ascending per-stratum/condition candidate consumption plus a two-phase deterministic allocation workflow. Does NOT touch any scientific predicate, support bound, token rule, physical guard, seed root, block definition, quota, or total.

trigger.deterministic_reproduction: three Stage-B batch attempts reproduced the failure identically (task 27 FAILED in each 50-task dispatch; 49/50 tasks done in each): results/dataset_v3/formal/pass1_stage_b_ood_a1.log, pass1_stage_b_ood_a2.log, pass1_stage_b_ood_a3.log; plus two single-task probes with identical outcome (100 attempts: 25 guard-band rejects + 75 no-target rejects + 0 STRESS_SET removals)

iid_rejection_gate_coincident_evidence.observed: verdict=FAIL; overall rejection_rate=0.1724 (<0.50) yet the per-stratum gate fired via candidate-window exhaustion; all 576/576 ACCEPT voyages are present and data-complete (ledger voyages: 576 entries, all ACCEPT)
iid_rejection_gate_coincident_evidence.interpretation: per-family window fragmentation artificially inflates per-stratum rejection accounting: the same disease as C1 k=6. IID support was never scientifically exhausted; only the private per-family windows were.

old_window_rule.rule: each (condition, family k) owned a private contiguous candidate window [base + k*W, base + (k+1)*W) of the frozen 1000-index block; W = floor(1000/16) = 62 (IID) / floor(1000/10) = 100 (OOD)
old_window_rule.advance_rule: "rejected attempts advance within the window only": a rejected candidate advanced the family cursor strictly inside its own private window; the window boundary was never crossed
old_window_rule.exhaustion_rule: window exhausted => slot_fails => UNREACHABLE for that family slot (same-seed retries confined to the same window)
old_window_rule.defect: scheduling-level local barrenness: candidate indices outside a family's private window were unreachable even though the same frozen 1000-index block still contained untried draws. UNREACHABLE verdicts produced by window exhaustion therefore did NOT imply scientific unreachability of the block.

new_allocation_rule.rule: per-family contiguous candidate-window ownership is RETIRED. For each stratum/condition, candidates are consumed in canonical ascending order starting from the frozen block head (base_draw_index ascending) until the preregistered quota is filled.
per_candidate_semantics: apply ALL frozen support / token REQUIRE / physical-domain / eligibility rules unchanged
record every rejection/disposition in the consumption ledger
FAILED_* disposition retried only per the existing same-seed retry policy
REJECTED_* disposition advances the cursor to the next candidate index
accept fills the family slot; once the quota is full, stop consuming
UNREACHABLE only when the ENTIRE 1000-index block is exhausted with the quota still unfilled (true block unreachability)
new_allocation_rule.reclassification: C1 k=6 failure is reclassified as ARTIFICIAL_SUPPORT_FRAGMENTATION_BY_PER_FAMILY_DRAW_WINDOW: a scheduling-level local-barrenness artifact of the retired window rule, NOT scientific unreachability of the C1 support

phase_s.property: selection semantics are independent of worker count and of completion order

phase_r.name: Phase R: simulation
phase_r.rule: workers simulate ONLY the accepted base draws listed in the plan; workers are FORBIDDEN from searching, resampling, or allocating on their own

two_phase_workflow.plan_reuse: the same plan drives pass1 and pass2 of the two-run determinism check

required_regression_invariants.name: true_block_unreachable

required_regression_invariants.name: unique_candidate_identity

required_regression_invariants.name: candidate_accounting_closure
required_regression_invariants.semantics: every candidate index in the consumed range carries exactly one final ledger disposition (ACCEPT / REJECTED_* / FAILED_*), and the ledger closes against the consumed range
